to prevent Baidu from crossing the mountains of Shahrazur.
After a few days, he also mounted his father-in-law,
a man named Aqbuqa,
with another myriad and sent him,
so that he himself would also take another myriad,
and go and meet Baidu.
And while he was still in the vicinity of Tabriz,
a place called Ujan,
Taghar and Aqbuqa arrived with the two myriads that were with them at the foot of Mount Shahrazur,
from the eastern side.
And Baidu likewise, with his own men, was at the foot of the mountain,
from the western side.
And he sent messengers secretly to Taghar, saying:
"Behold, I burn with the fire of zeal for the kingdom of the house of Magog;
and I strive to uproot Gaykhatu on account of the abominable {OCR?} qualities that are in him,
especially as I hear that he has not left you wives, sons, or daughters with whom he has not committed lewdness.
Therefore, all of us together in one agreement ought to unite and remove him from the midst,
and set Ghazan upon the throne of the kingdom,
and all of us submit to him equally."
Now Taghar readily welcomed this,
and easily joined with him.
And at that very hour he sent word to his companion Aqbuqa:
"I am with Baidu,
and I am in agreement with him,
and to him I am about to go.
What is your intention?" But because he was the father-in-law of Gaykhatu,
this did not please him,
and he was grieved and distressed.
And he thought that on that very night he would take the myriad {OCR?} that was with him,
and return to Gaykhatu.
And when the morning dawned,
Taghar rode as if he were going toward Baidu.
Aqbuqa thought that he was about to strike him,
so he abandoned everything and fled.
And a few from the myriad that was with him followed him,
and with swift feet he reached Gaykhatu,
and reported to him what had taken place.
Then terror fell upon Gaykhatu,
and he did not know what to do.
He sent and summoned the commander of the thousands that was with him,
whose name was Barim Brayem {OCR?}, and said to him:
"Behold, I see that my forces have been divided against me.
Henceforth, remain brave and agile,
and do not be divided!"
And he brought garments and clothed him.
he made him a commander of a myriad {OCR?}.
